question.text: The Aztecs, meanwhile, used this language, whose modern variety is still widely spoken today. The words "chipotle" and "axolotl" come from this language.
question.clue: Historians learned to write in this language at schools called calmecacs ("kahl-MAY-kahks").

swap.leadin: In trying to escape from the capital of this empire, Spanish soldiers experienced La Noche Triste [la no-chay tree-stay].
swap.text: Name this empire, led by Montezuma, which was conquered by Hernan Cortes in 1521.
swap.clue: One ruler of this empire targeted its neighbor during the Flower Wars.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the native peoples of the Americas.
question.text: Sites from this Mesoamerican civilization include La Venta and San Lorenzo, which were mysteriously abandoned. They created giant stone heads, thought to be depictions of their rulers.
question.clue: This culture created "elongated man" figurines as well as a greenstone statue of a man holding a were-jaguar ("wair-jaguar").

swap.leadin: The Soviet linguist Yuri Knorozov listed his cat Asya as the co-author of a paper in which he determined that this civilization's writing system was phonetic.
swap.text: Name this civilization centered around the Yucatan peninsula whose "long count" calendar had a b'ak'tun end in 2012.
swap.clue: The Temple of Inscriptions houses anajaw("ah-how")from this civilizationknown as Pacal the Great who reigned for 68 years in its city-state of Palenque("pah-LEN-kay").

question.text: This site, located in the Yucatan Peninsula in present day Mexico, is the site of a step pyramid known as the Temple of Kukulcan. This site contains an observatory referred to as El Caracol, and a Mayan ball game court.
question.clue: This location was once part of a league with neighboring Uxmal .

swap.text: The Colossal Heads were created by this earliest major civilization of Mesoamerica, who were the first to play the mesoamerican ballgame. This culture's writing system may have influenced the later Mayan hieroglyphics system.
swap.clue: This Mesoamerican civilization was the first to practice ritual bloodletting and play the ball game, according to artifacts found near their cities like San Lorenzo and La Venta.

question.leadin: In some ancient cultures, desperate times called for desperate measures.
question.text: This Mesoamerican culture performed a sacrifice at the peak of the New Fire ceremony, which was carried out every year to prevent the end of the world. They were later conquered by Hernan Cortez and his conquistadors.
question.clue: High ranking warriors of these people were named for eagles and jaguars, and fought with clubs embedded with obsidian called macuahuitl ("mah-kwah-hwee-tul").

swap.text: This Olmec site became important due to its abundant rainfall, which eliminated the need for an extensive irrigation system. It was located in modern-day Tabasco, and its Great Pyramid, due to erosion, is conical in shape.
swap.clue: Several colossal heads have been found in the sites of San Lorenzo, Tres Zapotes, and Complex B in this Olmec archaeological site in Tabasco. This site also contains the Great Pyramid.

question.text: Large numbers of children from this ethnic group were abducted after massacres carried out by forces loyal to Efrain Rios Montt in Guatemala. Rigoberta Menchu, a member of this indigenous group, won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992.
question.answerHtml: Maya [accept K'iche' Maya; prompt on indigenous peoples or Native Americans or Indians]
question.clue: Guatemala committed a genocide against this civilization, whose howler monkey gods were chronicled in the Popul Vuh.

swap.leadin: Alberto Ruz Lhuillier (lweel-YAY) was buried at this site in honor of his work excavating it, and Jean-Frederic Maximilien de Waldeck supposedly lived on top of its Temple of the Count for three years while illustrating its ruins.
swap.text: Identify this city that flourished during the Late Classic Period. A tomb was found beneath the Temple of the Inscriptions at this site in 1952.
swap.clue: The French explorer Jean-Frederic Waldeck resided for a time at this city, where a leafy corn plant mural is located at its "foliated cross" complex.

question.text: A concurrent city much further south in ancient Mexico was Monte Alban, the capital of this Mesoamerican culture whose writing system is still mostly untranslated.
question.clue: The chief god of this culture was the thunder god Cocijo.

swap.leadin: Civilizations utilizing this system also used a smaller-scale system with Haab' and Tzolk'in components.
swap.text: Identify this primarily base-20 system. The end of a b'ak'tun was predicted by this system's Long Count.
swap.clue: The Book of Chilam Balam of Chumayel discusses this system, which was split into the divine Tzolk'in and civil Haab' derived from "Venus rounds."

question.text: This conquistador contracted the scholar Francisco Lopez de Gomara to write an account of his conquest of Tenochtitlan ("teh-nohch-teet-LAHN").
question.answerHtml: Hernán Cortés [or Hernán Cortés de Monroy y Pizarro Altamirano]
question.clue: This man won the Battle of Otumba and fathered a child with his translator, La Malinche.

swap.leadin: This city's emblem glyph is the most widely distributed of all such glyphs in the Americas.
swap.text: Name this city whose ruler Sky Witness achieved a major power reversal by converting Caracol from a vassal of this city's rival Tikal into an ally. Today, this city is identified as the capital of the "Kingdom of the Snake."
swap.clue: This Snake Kingdom known for being the bitter enemy of Tikal during the Classical Mayan period.

question.leadin: This city's conquest by Calakmul marks the boundary between the Early Classic and Late Classic periods of Mesoamerican civilization.
question.text: Name this city home to a dynasty founded by Yax Ehb Xook, or First Step Shark.
question.clue: This polity's rival was called the Snake Kingdom, and this polity's namesake hiatus began after its ruler Wak Chan K'awiil was defeated by this polity's rival and Caracol.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about some North American ruins.
swap.text: This Mayan city is located in the western portion of Honduras. It was ruled by the awesomely named Xukpi Kingdom, as well as someone name 18 Rabbit.
swap.clue: An extremely long text comprised of over 2,000 glyphs is found at this site's "Hieroglyphic Stairway."

question.leadin: The ruler of this city, Hunac Ceel, supposedly convinced the ruler at Chichen Itza to steal the bride of Izamal, inciting a war that depopulated Chichen Itza.
question.text: Name this Mesoamerican site in the Yucatan that formed a namesake league of 16 city-states around 1280 AD under the Cocom family, which lasted until the revolt of the Xiu family.

swap.text: The nine books given this name are primary sources on Mayan religious tradition. Among their contents include prophecies and prognostications based on the k'atun cycle and riddles used to confirm public officials for office.

question.leadin: This historian's only written work was used by Tzevtan Todorov to argue that the "site of strategic symbolic occupation" was in the "body of a woman" that appeared in his major text.
question.text: Name this man, who described how the Tlaxcala allied themselves with Hernan Cortes's expedition in his book The True History of the Conquest of New Spain.

swap.text: This city and Chichen Itza were members of the league of Mayapan. It is home to the Pyramid of the Magician.
swap.clue: This site in the Yucatan Peninsula, which is thought to have been ruled by the Tutul Xiw people during its Golden Age from 700-1000 AD. Since it lacks continuous freshwater supply, several cisterns called chultuns were built at this site.
